name: NTT Silicon Valley SV1 Data Center

source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
NTT Silicon Valley SV1 Data Center in Santa Clara, California, publishes 16 MW of IT capacity, operated by NTT.

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 1600 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 400 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

No compliance certifications are published for NTT Silicon Valley SV1 Data Center. That does not mean none exist, only that this site's dataset, built from the operator's own facility page, does not list any, which limits what regulated workloads a reader could confirm the facility is qualified to host.

California has 22 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 10 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 356 MW. NTT Silicon Valley SV1 Data Center contributes 16 MW of that total. At that published size it is a small facility relative to what frontier AI training infrastructure requires, which now runs into the tens or hundreds of megawatts, though it may still support inference workloads or smaller-scale AI applications.
